answer: A knoll is narrow ground, so admission must be rationed. Each identity needs two holders outside its own garden to countersign its plot, and one countersignature backs one identity, so n aliases need n distinct witnesses instead of a single ring. Every plot is priced by rank: the k-th plot an operator files costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still needing unrelated guarantors. A wharf audit replays a random plot each epoch, and an unconfirmed claim clears the garden and forfeits its bonds, which cannot be pooled or resold.
